speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the current number of foreign remote employees hired by companies based in Singapore; (b) what is the number of foreign remote employees broken down by industry; and (c) what measures is the Ministry taking to discourage excessive offshoring of quality jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have seen in the past, activities such as garment manufacturing and call centre operations being offshored to lower cost locations.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: At the same time, our economy transformed and shifted towards higher value-added activities such as Advanced Manufacturing and Fintech.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This transformation created high value-added jobs in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The anchoring of global companies will help to preserve and also spur the creation of good jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Together with our tripartite partners, we will continue to help our local workforce to reskill and upskill for future jobs and skills.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: However, our success cannot be taken for granted.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This will mean fewer opportunities for future generations of Singaporeans and is certainly something that we would want to avoid.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: My supplementary question is as such: are such workers, foreign remote employees subject to foreign workforce levers such as levies and quotas, as well as CPF payments?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will there be plans for them to subject to such levers and CPF payments in the future?
